effects: The user's Silhouette becomes S3 unless their profile Silhouette is higher.
The user has Partial Cover in a 360-degree arc and gains [[skill:mimetism]] (-3) and [[skill:courage]] while the State is active.
The user cannot perform movement while Foxhole State remains active.
requirements: Foxhole State is entered through [[skill:sapper]] and requires space for the State's Silhouette.
restrictions: Entering [[state:prone]] cancels Foxhole State.
In the Active Turn, declaring a Movement-labelled Skill or beginning a [[skill:dodge]] move can cancel Foxhole State before that movement.

records.name: Berserk
records.summary: A Long CC Special Skill that combines an extended [[skill:move]] with a [[skill:cc-attack]] against a visible target.

requirements: The target must be inside the user's Line of Fire when Berserk is declared.
effects: The user declares [[skill:move]] and [[skill:cc-attack]] as one Long Skill and may move up to the sum of both MOV values to reach Silhouette contact with the target.
If the target cannot be reached, the declaration becomes [[skill:idle]] and neither the [[skill:move]] nor the [[skill:cc-attack]] is performed.
A Berserk MOD shown in the Unit Profile applies to the [[skill:cc-attack]].
restrictions: The user declares the movement route and [[skill:cc-attack]] target before ARO declarations.

records.name: Guard
records.summary: An Automatic CC Special Skill that lets the user make a [[skill:cc-attack]] against a target in Line of Fire and Zone of Control without Silhouette contact.

requirements: The [[skill:cc-attack]] target must be inside the user’s Line of Fire and Zone of Control.
effects: The user may perform a [[skill:cc-attack]] without reaching or being in Silhouette contact with the target.
The user and target may apply Skills and MODs whose normal requirements include Silhouette contact.
restrictions: Guard cannot be used against an active [[skill:aerial]] Trooper unless that Trooper is [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]].

records.name: Neurocinetics
records.summary: An Automatic Special Skill that shifts BS Weapon Burst from the Active Turn to the Reactive Turn.

effects: During the Active Turn, the Burst of all the user’s BS Weapons is reduced to 1.
During the Reactive Turn, the user may apply each BS Weapon’s full Burst against a single target.
Burst MODs apply in the Reactive Turn instead of the Active Turn.

records.name: Total Reaction
records.summary: An Automatic Special Skill that lets [[skill:bs-attack]] AROs use a weapon’s full Burst against one activated target.

effects: When declaring a [[skill:bs-attack]] ARO, the user may apply the full Burst of the selected weapon, including Burst MODs.
restrictions: The ARO must target one of the Troopers activated by the Order.

records.name: Triangulated Fire
records.summary: A Long Attack Skill that performs a [[skill:bs-attack]] without applying Roll MODs other than Burst MODs.

requirements: The user must have Line of Fire to the target.
effects: The user performs a [[skill:bs-attack]] without applying Range, Cover, or Special Skill MODs to the Roll.
Burst MODs are still applied normally.
restrictions: The attack cannot target beyond the selected weapon’s Maximum Range.

records.name: Aerial
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill representing a Trooper whose flight prevents normal contact and several ground-based interactions.

effects: While Aerial is active, the user is never in Silhouette contact with other Models, Objectives, scenery items, or game elements, even if physically touching them.
restrictions: While Aerial is active, the user cannot be in [[state:prone]] or [[state:engaged]].
The user cannot declare [[skill:cautious-movement]].
[[skill:guard]] cannot be used against the user unless the user is [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]].
Weapons with the [[trait:boost|Boost]] Trait do not activate against the user.

records.name: Climbing Plus
records.summary: An optional Automatic Movement Special Skill that makes [[skill:climb]] faster to declare and extends normal movement actions onto vertical surfaces.

requirements: At the end of the movement, the user must be able to place itself on a surface at least as large as its base.
effects: If declared as the first Basic Short Skill of the Order, [[skill:climb]] is treated as a Basic Short Skill instead of a Long Skill.
The user may move on vertical surfaces as though they were horizontal while declaring [[skill:move]] or [[skill:dodge]], and while moving because of a failed Guts Roll.
The user may declare other compatible Basic Short Skills or Short Skills while moving on a vertical surface or hanging from a height.
During the Reactive Turn, the user may declare an ARO while on a vertical surface when otherwise permitted.
restrictions: [[skill:climb]] can be declared as a Basic Short Skill only once per Order; a following [[skill:move]] uses the second MOV value.
The user cannot benefit from Partial Cover MODs while on a vertical surface.
Troopers cannot deploy on vertical surfaces during the Deployment Phase or during the game.

records.name: Terrain
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that improves movement in one matching Terrain Type, or every Terrain Type with Terrain (Total).

requirements: The Terrain area must match a Terrain Type listed by the user’s Terrain Special Skill.
effects: When declaring a Skill with the Movement Label inside a matching Terrain area, the user gains [[distance:+1:inch]] to the first value of its MOV Attribute.
The user may move normally through matching Terrain areas without applying that Terrain area’s movement restrictions.
If several Terrain Types are listed, the player chooses one when placing the Trooper on the game table.
Terrain (Total) applies these effects to every Terrain Type defined by the rules.

records.name: Warhorse
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that keeps the user operational through Loss of Lieutenant, Retreat, Isolation, and certain [[skill:bs-attack]] penalties.

effects: The user is not affected by Loss of Lieutenant and remains Regular.
The user is not affected by Retreat, remains Regular, and does not enter [[state:retreat|Retreat State]].
The user cannot enter [[state:isolated]].
[[skill:bs-attack]] (-X) Special Skill MODs have no effect against the user.

records.name: Courage
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that lets the user choose to automatically pass Guts Rolls and remain operational during Retreat.

effects: The user may choose to automatically pass any Guts Roll.
The user is unaffected by Retreat situations, cannot enter [[state:retreat|Retreat State]], and acts normally until the end of the game.
restrictions: The user is still affected by Loss of Lieutenant, including during Retreat.

records.name: Frenzy
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that, after the user directly wounds or kills an enemy, grants [[skill:impetuous]] and [[skill:limited-cover]] and removes Marker States.

requirements: The user must directly inflict at least one Wound on an Enemy Trooper or cause that Trooper to enter [[state:dead]].
effects: In the States Phase of the Player Turn where the Requirement is met, the user gains [[skill:impetuous]] and [[skill:limited-cover]] and retains them for the remainder of the game.
When the user gains [[skill:impetuous]] through Frenzy, they cancel any Marker State they are in and cannot re-enter those States.
restrictions: Wounds caused by the user’s Weapons with the [[trait:deployable]] Trait do not satisfy the Requirement.

records.name: Impetuous
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that grants one activation in the Impetuous Phase while tightly constraining its legal Skill combinations and movement.

effects: During the Tactical Phase, place an Impetuous Token next to the user; during the Impetuous Phase the user may activate once by removing that Token without spending an Order.
An Impetuous activation follows the normal Order Expenditure Sequence and permits only the Skill combinations listed by the rule.
Movement-labelled Skills declared in the Impetuous Phase must follow the rule’s mandatory movement priorities and normally use the full corresponding MOV value.
restrictions: In the Impetuous Phase, [[skill:move]], [[skill:jump]], or [[skill:climb]] cancels [[state:prone]] and the user cannot enter [[state:prone]] at the end of the movement.
Impetuous Troopers cannot enter Marker States or any other States that explicitly prohibit entry.
A player in Retreat does not carry out the Impetuous Phase.

records.name: Religious Troop
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that automatically passes Guts Rolls while allowing a WIP Roll to apply failed-Guts movement, and ignores Retreat.

effects: The user automatically passes Guts Rolls and therefore normally holds position after surviving an Attack.
The user may instead make a WIP Roll; on success, they may apply the effects of failing the Guts Roll.
The user is unaffected by Retreat situations, does not enter [[state:retreat|Retreat State]], and acts normally until the end of the game.
restrictions: During Retreat, the user cannot voluntarily leave the game table unless scenario rules allow it.
The user remains affected by Loss of Lieutenant, including during Retreat.

records.name: Dead State
records.summary: An irreversible Null State entered after a Trooper receives more Wounds than its VITA or STR value.

effects: The Trooper is removed from the game table and its Combat Group.
The Trooper no longer generates Orders and does not count toward Victory Points.
requirements: The Trooper has received more Wounds than its VITA or STR value, including receiving further Wounds while [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]].
restrictions: Dead State is irreversible unless a mission or scenario rule explicitly provides a cancellation procedure.

records.name: Engaged State
records.summary: A close-combat State entered through Silhouette contact with an eligible enemy Trooper.

effects: The Trooper is considered to be in Close Combat.
The Trooper may only declare [[skill:berserk]], [[skill:cc-attack]], [[skill:dodge]], [[skill:idle]], [[skill:reset]], or Skills that explicitly allow use in Close Combat or Engaged State.
The Trooper cannot draw Line of Fire outside its Close Combat.
requirements: The Trooper is in Silhouette contact with an enemy and neither Trooper is Immobilized or in a Null State, except [[state:sepsitorized|Sepsitorized]] or [[state:possessed|Possessed]].

records.name: Holoecho State
records.summary: A Marker State created by [[equipment:holoprojector]] that conceals which of up to three representations is the real bearer.

effects: The bearer is represented together with holographic decoys and the player records which representation is real as Private Information.
The bearer and Holoechoes act together when the bearer is activated.
Enemies must [[skill:discover]] the relevant representation to reveal the bearer without another cancellation condition.
requirements: [[equipment:holoprojector]] places or restores the Holoechoes under the deployment, States Phase, or Active Turn conditions specified by the rule.
restrictions: Holoecho State is canceled by its listed revelation and coherency conditions, including declarations or events that reveal the bearer.

records.name: HoloMask State
records.summary: A disguise State that represents the bearer as another same-faction Trooper while retaining the bearer’s real profile.

effects: The bearer is represented by an imitated same-faction or same-Sectorial Trooper with the same Silhouette value.
The bearer continues to use its real Unit Profile.
A successful [[skill:discover]] replaces the imitated Model with the real Model.
requirements: The imitated Trooper must belong to the bearer’s faction or Sectorial Army and have the same Silhouette value.
restrictions: A Trooper in [[state:holomask|HoloMask State]] cannot copy [[skill:hacker]] or Hackable status or items with the [[trait:deployable]] Trait represented by Tokens or Models.
The State is canceled by its listed revelation conditions.

records.name: Normal State
records.summary: The default State for Troopers and game elements unless another rule specifies otherwise.

effects: The Trooper normally generates an Order during the Tactical Phase.
The Trooper counts toward its player’s Victory Points.
requirements: Troopers normally deploy in this State and return to it when their Null State is canceled unless another rule applies.
restrictions: Normal State is canceled when the Trooper enters a Null State or another rule explicitly says so.

records.name: Prone State
records.summary: A posture State that changes Silhouette and halves Movement-labelled movement while active.

effects: The Trooper uses Silhouette X, matching the height and width of its base.
Movement from Skills with the Movement Label and failed Guts Rolls is halved while Prone.
requirements: A Trooper may deploy Prone or change between [[state:normal|Normal]] and Prone at the permitted points of Movement-labelled Skills or AROs; eligible Troopers also become Prone when entering [[state:unconscious]].
restrictions: [[skill:jump]] cancels Prone State, and some troop types or Equipment cannot enter Prone State.

records.name: Possessed State
records.summary: A Null State in which control of the affected Trooper passes to the opposing player and the Possessed profile is used.

effects: The owning player cannot activate the Trooper or give it Orders from the owner’s Order Pool.
The opposing player that caused the State may activate it through that Trooper’s Combat Group, using the Possessed profile.
The Trooper contributes no Orders, counts for neither player’s Victory Points, and cannot belong to a Fireteam.
requirements: A successful Attack, Effect, Hacking Program, scenario rule, or other game condition capable of causing Possessed State affects the Trooper.
restrictions: The owning player may cancel Possessed State with a Command Token in the specified Tactical Phase step, and [[hacking-program:total-control]] can also cancel it.

records.name: Retreat! State
records.summary: A State applied when an army enters Retreat! that restricts declarations and cancels Marker and holographic States.

effects: The Trooper may only use Basic Short Skills, [[skill:cautious-movement]], [[skill:dodge]], [[skill:reset]], or Special Skills that explicitly permit use in Retreat!.
Entering Retreat! cancels [[equipment:holoprojector]] and [[state:holomask|HoloMask State]] presentation and Marker States.
requirements: The Trooper’s army enters the Retreat! situation at the beginning of the Player Turn.
restrictions: Troopers protected by [[skill:courage]], [[skill:religious-troop]], [[skill:warhorse]], or another applicable rule do not enter Retreat! State.

records.name: Sepsitorized State
records.summary: A Null State caused by a failed Saving Roll against [[weapon:sepsitor|Sepsitor]] that transfers practical control of the Trooper to the opposing player.

effects: The Trooper leaves its original Combat Group and cannot receive Orders from its owner.
The opposing player that caused the State may activate the Trooper through that Trooper’s Combat Group.
The Trooper contributes no Orders, counts for neither player’s Victory Points, and cannot belong to a Fireteam.
requirements: A Cube-wearing Trooper fails a Saving Roll against a [[weapon:sepsitor|Sepsitor]] Attack.

records.name: Suppressive Fire State
records.summary: A combat State entered through the [[skill:suppressive-fire]] Skill that uses the weapon’s SF Mode and penalizes nearby enemy Face to Face Rolls.

effects: Enemies within [[distance:24:inch]] apply a -3 MOD to their Attribute in Face to Face Rolls against the Trooper.
The selected weapon uses its Suppressive Fire Mode and may react in ARO with the full B3 against one target.
requirements: The Trooper declared the [[skill:suppressive-fire]] Long Skill.
restrictions: The State is canceled by the listed Order, ARO, weapon, Guts Roll, State, Loss of Lieutenant, or Fireteam conditions.

records.name: Dogged
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that lets an [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] Trooper keep acting temporarily before entering [[state:dead]].

requirements: The user must enter [[state:unconscious]] and declare Dogged immediately, in either the Active or Reactive Turn.
effects: While Dogged is active, ignore the effects and Null Label of [[state:unconscious]] and treat the Trooper as being in [[state:normal]] for the rest of that Player Turn.
In the States Phase of that Player Turn, the Trooper automatically enters [[state:dead]].
If the Trooper receives another Wound while Dogged is active, it enters [[state:dead]] directly.
A [[skill:remote-presence]] Trooper with STR may activate Dogged when entering any level of [[state:unconscious]].
restrictions: Once Dogged is activated, the Trooper cannot be healed.
A [[skill:remote-presence]] Trooper cannot activate Dogged merely because it was already in [[state:unconscious]] before the triggering event.

records.name: No Wound Incapacitation
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that lets an [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] Trooper ignore that State's normal restrictions while remaining healable.

requirements: The user must enter [[state:unconscious]] and declare No Wound Incapacitation immediately, in either the Active or Reactive Turn.
effects: While active, ignore the effects and Null Label of [[state:unconscious]] and treat the Trooper as being in [[state:normal]].
The user can be healed; removing one Wound returns it to [[state:normal]] and removes the NWI Token.
A [[skill:remote-presence]] Trooper with STR may activate No Wound Incapacitation when entering any level of [[state:unconscious]].
A user that also has [[skill:doctor]] or [[skill:engineer]] may use that Skill on itself, applying the corresponding Effects.
restrictions: If the user receives another Wound, it enters [[state:dead]] directly.
If a Roll to heal the user fails, it enters [[state:dead]] directly.
A [[skill:remote-presence]] Trooper cannot activate No Wound Incapacitation merely because it was already in [[state:unconscious]] before the triggering event.

records.name: Remote Presence
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill for STR Troopers that adds a second [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] level and changes repair behavior.

effects: A Remote Presence Trooper with STR has two distinct levels of [[state:unconscious]] before entering [[state:dead]].
From either [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] level, one successful [[skill:engineer]] WIP Roll or [[equipment:gizmokit]] PH Roll removes all Wounds necessary to cancel [[state:unconscious]].
When [[skill:engineer]] or another rule explicitly permits it, Command Tokens may reroll the failed repair Roll.
Remote Presence remains active while its owner is in a Null State.
restrictions: The second [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] level applies to Troopers with both Remote Presence and the STR Attribute.

records.name: Shasvastii
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that changes how a Shasvastii Trooper's [[state:unconscious]] counts for Victory Point conditions during the game.

requirements: The user must enter [[state:unconscious]] and activate Shasvastii immediately, in either the Active or Reactive Turn.
effects: While the Shasvastii-Embryo form is active, the [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] Trooper still counts when calculating Victory Points for Retreat and other scenario rules or conditions.
At the end of the game, these special [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] rules end and the Trooper no longer counts when calculating Victory Points.

records.name: Regeneration
records.summary: An optional States Phase Automatic Special Skill that makes a PH Roll to remove a Wound, potentially cancelling [[state:unconscious]].

effects: During the States Phase, the user makes a Normal PH Roll.
On success, remove one Wound and cancel [[state:unconscious]] if applicable.
On failure, the user receives one additional Wound.
Regeneration remains active while its owner is in a Null State.

records.name: Protheion
records.summary: An optional Automatic CC Special Skill that converts Wounds inflicted in Close Combat into recovered Wounds or temporary VITA increases.

requirements: The user must be in Silhouette contact with a target that has VITA and declare a [[skill:cc-attack]].
effects: For each Wound inflicted on the target by the user's [[skill:cc-attack]], or each Coup de Grâce performed, remove one Wound the user has received.
If the user has no Wounds to remove, remaining eligible Wounds increase VITA by one each, to a maximum of two points above the original value.
When Wounds are inflicted both by and on the user in the same Order, Protheion recovery and VITA increases are resolved before Wounds inflicted on the user.
restrictions: VITA can be increased by at most two points above the user's original value.

records.name: Loss of Lieutenant
records.summary: An army-level situation declared when the active player lacks an operational deployed [[skill:lieutenant]] during the Tactical Phase.

requirements: During the Tactical Phase, the active player has no deployed [[skill:lieutenant]] because the [[skill:lieutenant]] is absent, [[state:isolated|Isolated]], or in a Null State.
effects: All Troopers in the Army List are Irregular while the Loss of Lieutenant situation applies.
At the end of the Turn, the player appoints a new eligible [[skill:lieutenant]] at no cost, canceling the situation.
restrictions: Troopers with Irregular Training or the REM Troop Type cannot be appointed as the replacement [[skill:lieutenant]].

records.name: Regular Order
records.summary: An Order contributed by a Regular Trooper to its Combat Group's Order Pool, where it may be spent to activate Troopers in that Combat Group.

effects: The Order contributed by a Regular Trooper is added to its Combat Group's Order Pool.
A Regular Order in that Order Pool may be spent to activate any Trooper in the same Combat Group.

records.name: Irregular Order
records.summary: An Order contributed by an Irregular Trooper and kept separate from the Combat Group Order Pool for that Trooper's own use.

effects: The Order contributed by an Irregular Trooper is kept by that Trooper for their own use.
An Irregular Trooper may still spend Regular Orders from its Combat Group's Order Pool.
restrictions: An Irregular Order is not added to the Combat Group's Order Pool.

records.name: Special Lieutenant Order
records.summary: A special Order generated for the [[skill:lieutenant]] and kept separate from the Combat Group Order Pool for the [[skill:lieutenant]]'s own use.

effects: The Order is kept separate from the Order Pool for the [[skill:lieutenant]]'s own use.
Its status and expenditure are Open Information.
restrictions: The Special Lieutenant Order is not part of an Order Pool.

records.name: Tactical Order
records.summary: A special Order kept by the Trooper that generates it, usable by that Trooper and by applicable advanced rules such as Fireteams.

effects: A Tactical Order is kept by the Trooper that generates it for that Trooper's own use.
Applicable advanced rules may allow the Tactical Order to activate a Fireteam.
restrictions: A Tactical Order is not added to an Order Pool.

records.name: Command Token: Strategic Use
records.summary: The Strategic Use mode of Command Tokens, covering first-turn procedural effects and the Speedball logistical option.

effects: Strategic Use can alter Deployment, remove Regular Orders, limit enemy Command Token use, place a Trooper into [[state:suppressive-fire]], or grant Speedball Tokens according to the selected option.
restrictions: Each player may spend at most two Command Tokens for Strategic Use: one Procedural option and one Logistical option.

records.name: Chain of Command
records.summary: An optional private Automatic Special Skill that appoints its user as the new [[skill:lieutenant]] when the current [[skill:lieutenant]] is unavailable during the Loss of Lieutenant check.

requirements: Use only at the start of the player's Loss of Lieutenant check.
The current [[skill:lieutenant]] must be [[state:isolated|Isolated]] or in a Null State.
The user must be on the table as a Model or Marker and cannot be [[state:isolated|Isolated]] or in a Null State.
effects: The user becomes the new [[skill:lieutenant]] and gains the [[skill:lieutenant]] Special Skill with no additional abilities.
The Loss of Lieutenant check is successful for the Turn.
restrictions: Chain of Command (Non Specialist) does not grant Specialist Troop status in scenarios where ordinary Chain of Command would do so.

records.name: Counterintelligence
records.summary: An optional private Automatic Special Skill that reduces the opponent's first-turn Command Token Strategic Use effects.

effects: Reduce to one the number of Orders the adversary can nullify with Strategic Use of a Command Token.
Alternatively, increase to two the number of Command Tokens the adversary may use when Strategic Use would otherwise limit them to one.

records.name: Inspiring Leadership
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that, while its user is the active [[skill:lieutenant]], grants army-wide Training and [[skill:courage]] effects plus command benefits.

effects: If the user is [[skill:lieutenant]], on the table, and not in a Null State, all Order-providing Troopers gain Regular Training and [[skill:courage]] except that [[skill:religious-troop]] does not receive the granted [[skill:courage]] effect.
The Special Lieutenant Order may be used to declare a Coordinated Order including the user without the normal Command Token or extra Order expenditure.
The army is unaffected by Retreat! while the active [[skill:lieutenant]] conditions are met.
A qualifying all-Regular Fireteam containing the user receives a [[distance:+2:inch]] Team Leader Zone of Control bonus for Coherency Checks.
restrictions: The Fireteam Coherency bonus is not cumulative with another Team Leader Zone of Control bonus.

records.name: Lieutenant
records.summary: An obligatory private Automatic Special Skill identifying the army's commanding officer and granting the Special Lieutenant Order.

effects: The user has a Special Lieutenant Order.
If the Lieutenant is absent from the table, [[state:isolated|Isolated]], or in a Null State during the Tactical Phase, Loss of Lieutenant applies.
The Lieutenant Skill remains active while its owner is in a Null State until a new Lieutenant is appointed.
restrictions: An Army List must include exactly one Lieutenant.
Irregular Troops and REM Troop Types cannot be chosen as Lieutenant.

records.name: Mnemonica
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that transfers the user's WIP, Mnemonica, and any [[skill:lieutenant]] status to an eligible allied host when the user enters a Null State.

requirements: The user must enter a Null State.
The chosen allied host must be on the battlefield as a Model or Marker and have either a [[equipment:cube]] or the REM Troop Type.
effects: Transfer the user's WIP value and Mnemonica to the chosen host; if the user was [[skill:lieutenant]], transfer [[skill:lieutenant]] and its additional abilities as well.
The transfer completes automatically at the end of the Order in which the user entered the Null State.
After the transfer, the original user enters [[state:dead]] and is removed from the game table.
restrictions: Troopers with Mnemonica are never considered to have a [[equipment:cube]].

records.name: NCO
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that converts Special Lieutenant Orders into Tactical Orders for the NCO to use.

effects: Replace any Special Lieutenant Orders with Tactical Orders and use them.
The NCO and [[skill:lieutenant]] do not need to be in the same Combat Group.
An NCO acting as Fireteam Team Leader may use the resulting Tactical Order to activate the Fireteam.
restrictions: An [[state:isolated|Isolated]] NCO cannot replace Special Lieutenant Orders or use the resulting Tactical Orders.

records.name: Tactical Awareness
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that grants its user an additional Tactical Order.

effects: The user gains a Tactical Order in addition to the Order provided by Training.
Place the Tactical Order during Order Count when the user is on the table as a Model or Marker, or when the user is placed on the table during the Orders Phase.
A user acting as Fireteam Team Leader may spend this Tactical Order to activate the Fireteam.

records.name: Paramedic
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that equips the user with a [[equipment:medikit]] for recovering [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] allies.

effects: The user is equipped with a [[equipment:medikit]] to recover allied Troopers from [[state:unconscious]].

records.name: Tech-Recovery
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that lets an allied [[equipment:gizmokit]] cancel Engineer-recoverable States through the user’s PH Roll.

requirements: The user must be in a State that can be canceled by [[skill:engineer]].
An allied [[equipment:gizmokit]] must successfully hit the user or be applied through Silhouette contact.
effects: A successful Normal PH Roll cancels all of the user’s States that [[skill:engineer]] can cancel, except [[state:unconscious]].
A failed PH Roll has no negative consequence and the recovery can be tried again in a later Order.
If the user has a [[equipment:gizmokit]] PH value listed in its Unit Profile, use that PH value when a [[equipment:gizmokit]] is used on the user.
Tech-Recovery remains active while the user is in a Null State.
restrictions: Tech-Recovery does not cancel [[state:unconscious]]; resolve the [[equipment:gizmokit]] using its normal Unconscious-recovery rules instead.

records.name: Technorganic
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that allows an [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] Trooper to be recovered by medical or engineering methods regardless of VITA or STR.

requirements: The user must be in [[state:unconscious]].
effects: [[skill:doctor]], [[skill:engineer]], [[equipment:medikit]], and [[equipment:gizmokit]] may cancel the user’s [[state:unconscious]] regardless of whether the user has the VITA or STR Attribute.
Technorganic remains active while the user is in a Null State.
restrictions: Outside [[state:unconscious]], Technorganic does not extend those recovery methods beyond their normal VITA or STR applicability.

records.name: FT Master
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that regularizes the user's Fireteam during Order Count and can improve its Coherency when its members are already Regular.

requirements: The user must be part of a Fireteam.
effects: During Order Count, all members of the user's Fireteam are Regular while the user is part of that Fireteam.
If every Fireteam member already has the Regular Characteristic, add [[distance:2:inch]] to the Team Leader's Zone of Control for Fireteam Coherency Checks.
restrictions: The Coherency bonus is not cumulative with another bonus to the Team Leader's Zone of Control.
If the Skill names a Unit in brackets and the Fireteam contains a member of that Unit, the Fireteam is canceled if the FT Master leaves the Fireteam.

records.name: Number 2
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that can take over as Fireteam Team Leader when the current leader becomes [[state:isolated|Isolated]] or enters a Null State.

requirements: The user must be part of a Fireteam.
That Fireteam's current Team Leader must enter [[state:isolated]] or a Null State.
effects: The user may automatically become the new Fireteam Team Leader.
The user remains Team Leader even if the previous Team Leader recovers, until the player chooses another Team Leader.

records.name: Specialist Operative
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that makes its user a Specialist Troop for scenario rules even without another qualifying specialist role.

effects: In missions and scenarios, the user is considered a Specialist Troop and may use rules that apply to Specialist Troops.
This Specialist Troop status does not require the user to have another specialist role such as [[skill:engineer]], [[skill:doctor]], or [[skill:hacker]].

records.name: Journalist
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that modifies nearby allied and enemy Guts Rolls and can provide campaign bonuses while the Journalist remains operational.

effects: Troopers inside an allied Journalist's Zone of Control apply +3 to their Guts Rolls.
Troopers inside an enemy Journalist's Zone of Control apply -3 to their Guts Rolls.
In campaign play, an eligible Journalist grants +3 to CUBEVAC Rolls and Promotion Rolls at the end of a scenario.
restrictions: Campaign bonuses require the Journalist to remain on the game table in a non-Null State at the end of the scenario.
Multiple Journalist modifiers do not stack.

records.name: TAGCom
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that applies the user's profile-listed support MODs to TAGs in the same Combat Group while the user is operational.

effects: While the user is deployed on the table in a non-Null State, TAGs in the user's Combat Group receive the MODs listed in brackets with TAGCom on the user's Unit Profile.
restrictions: Identical TAGCom MODs are not cumulative; only different MODs may be applied together.

records.name: Booty
records.summary: An optional Deployment Skill that gives the user a random extra item or profile bonus from the Booty Chart after the Trooper is placed in Model form.

requirements: The Booty roll is made after the Trooper has been placed in Model form on the table.
effects: The user rolls once on the Booty Chart to determine an extra item or profile bonus.
An item obtained from the Booty Chart is added to the Trooper's existing weapons and Equipment rather than replacing them.

records.name: MetaChemistry
records.summary: An optional Deployment Skill that gives the user a random Attribute MOD or Special Skill from the MetaChemistry Chart after the Trooper is placed in Model form.

requirements: The MetaChemistry roll is made immediately after the Trooper has been placed in Model form on the table.
effects: The user may roll once on the MetaChemistry Chart to determine an extra Attribute MOD or Special Skill.
A Special Skill obtained from the MetaChemistry Chart is added to the Trooper's existing Skills rather than replacing them.

records.name: Explode
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Attack Skill that detonates when the user enters [[state:unconscious]], resolves a Shock Direct Template Attack, and then sends the user to [[state:dead]].

requirements: The user must be in [[state:unconscious]] for Explode to activate.
effects: Explode activates automatically when the user enters [[state:unconscious]].
At the end of that Order, before Guts Rolls, the user makes a Direct Template Attack centered on its base with PS 7 [[ammunition:shock|Shock Ammunition]] against ARM.
Enemy Troopers affected by the Attack that declared [[skill:dodge]] avoid it if they passed their PH Roll.
After the Rolls are resolved, the user enters [[state:dead]] and is removed from the game table.
restrictions: Explode does not activate if the user enters [[state:dead]] directly instead of entering [[state:unconscious]].
If the user activates [[skill:dogged]] or [[skill:no-wound-incapacitation]] when entering [[state:unconscious]], Explode does not activate.
If the template would affect an allied Model or Marker, the Template Attack is canceled, but the user still enters [[state:dead]].

records.name: Exrah
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that causes an Exrah Trooper entering [[state:unconscious]] to pass directly to [[state:dead]], preventing later recovery.

effects: If the user enters [[state:unconscious]], it automatically passes directly to [[state:dead]] without receiving an additional Wound and is removed from the game table.
Because the user passes directly to [[state:dead]], it cannot subsequently be healed by [[skill:doctor]], [[equipment:medikit]], [[skill:regeneration]], or another recovery method.
Exrah remains active while its owner is in a Null State.

records.name: Immunity
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill whose profile-listed category changes or ignores specified Ammunition, Traits, States, or Critical-hit effects when the matching condition applies.

requirements: Immunity activates when the user must make a Saving Roll, or when the user is affected by the State named by an applicable Immunity (State) variant.
effects: The value in brackets on the Unit Profile determines which Ammunition, Trait, State, Attribute-based protection, or Critical-hit effect the Immunity applies to.
Immunity (Trait) ignores the special effects of the listed Trait.
Immunity (Ammunition) treats the listed Ammunition as Normal Ammunition, ignoring its special effects and its MODs to the Saving Roll Attribute and number of Saving Rolls.
Immunity (ARM) or (BTS) treats Ammunition that uses the named Saving Roll Attribute as Normal Ammunition; Immunity (Enhanced) combines both protections.
Immunity (State) prevents the listed State from being caused by Comms Attacks or special rule effects.
Immunity (Critical) removes the additional Saving Roll normally caused by a Critical hit.

For the reviewed [[ammunition:ap|AP]]+[[ammunition:da|DA]] case, Immunity (AP) negates AP’s ARM modifier, but not DA’s two Saving Rolls: the attack has two rolls against full ARM, or three for a Critical. This is a rule-derived case, not a separately printed example.
restrictions: Except for Immunity (State), Immunity does not apply against Comms Attacks.
Immunity does not prevent the [[trait:non-lethal|Non-Lethal]] or [[trait:state|State: Stunned]] Traits, which are always applied.
Unless the user has Immunity (Critical), a Critical hit still causes its additional Saving Roll even when the underlying Ammunition or effect is otherwise covered by Immunity.

records.name: Vulnerability
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that disables the user’s [[skill:immunity]] against the profile-listed Attack, weapon, or Ammunition.

effects: The value in brackets on the Unit Profile identifies an Attack, weapon, or Ammunition to which the user is vulnerable.
When facing that listed Attack, weapon, or Ammunition, the user cannot apply its [[skill:immunity]] Special Skill.

In the N5.3 source example, Vulnerability (Viral) prevents using [[skill:immunity|Immunity]] (Enhanced) against a weapon with Viral in its name. This example does not define a generic combined-ammunition component rule.

records.name: G: Jumper
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that represents one Trooper through two or three Proxy Models, with only one Proxy fully active at a time.

requirements: The player must enlist either two or three Proxies available to the G: Jumper Trooper.
All Proxies of the G: Jumper Trooper must belong to the same Combat Group, where they count as one Trooper.
effects: The user is represented by several Proxy Models but provides only one Order regardless of how many Proxies are deployed.
During the Active Turn, the player chooses the Proxy that becomes Active when declaring the Order; only that Active Proxy can declare Orders.
During the Reactive Turn, only one eligible Proxy becomes Active for the Order and reacts normally; other reacting Proxies may only declare [[skill:dodge]] or [[skill:reset]].
If the Active Proxy enters [[state:isolated]] or any Null State, the Active Proxy may be moved to another Proxy that is not in one of those States at the end of the Order.
Marker and [[state:hidden-deployment|Hidden Deployment]] status are not canceled merely by placing or assigning the Active Proxy Token.
Moving the G: Jumper Trooper between Combat Groups moves all of its Proxies together.
restrictions: A Proxy in [[state:isolated]] or any Null State cannot be activated until that State is canceled.
If all Proxies are in [[state:isolated]] or any Null State, the G: Jumper Trooper is treated as a casualty until at least one Proxy recovers.

records.name: Infinity Spec-Ops
records.summary: An optional Automatic Special Skill that lets a player customize one Spec-Ops Trooper during Army List creation and later replace its Initial Profile with its Enhanced Profile through SpecBall support.

effects: During Army List creation, the player selects one normal Skill, Weapon, or Equipment option and two different options from the Spec-Ops Chart.
The selected Spec-Ops Chart options apply to both the Initial Profile and the Enhanced Profile.
The Trooper always deploys using its Initial Profile and may replace it with the Enhanced Profile by collecting its SpecBall through the Request SpecBall rules.
Wounds and applicable States are shared between the Initial and Enhanced Profiles.
restrictions: An Army List cannot include more than one Trooper with Infinity Spec-Ops.
The current ITS season does not allow the use of Spec-Ops rules in official tournaments.

records.name: Morpho-Scan
records.summary: An optional no-roll Comms Attack that permanently replaces the user's MOV, CC, BS, and PH values with those of an eligible enemy Model in Zone of Control.

requirements: The target must be an enemy Model with the VITA Attribute in the user's Zone of Control.
effects: Morpho-Scan requires no Roll.
The user's MOV, CC, BS, and PH Attribute values are replaced by the target's corresponding values.
If the target declares [[skill:reset]] as an ARO to prevent Morpho-Scan, that [[skill:reset]] suffers a -9 MOD even without Line of Fire.
After Morpho-Scan successfully replaces the user's Attribute values, it cannot be used again during the game.
restrictions: Morpho-Scan has no effect on enemy Markers or enemy Troopers with the STR Attribute.

records.name: RemDriver
records.summary: An optional Deployment Skill that assigns the user's profile-listed MODs to one deployed Remote in the same Army List while the RemDriver remains operational.

effects: When the user is deployed, the player places a RemDriver Token beside one Remote already deployed on the game table.
The Remote with that Token receives the MODs shown in round brackets in the RemDriver user's Unit Profile.
restrictions: A Remote cannot have more than one RemDriver Token.
The RemDriver Token is removed at the end of the Order in which the user enters any Null State.

records.name: Transmutation
records.summary: An Automatic Special Skill family that changes a Trooper between Unit Profiles according to the listed Transmutation variant while sharing Wounds and applicable States across those profiles.

requirements: The user must satisfy the trigger or condition specified by the Transmutation variant shown in brackets on the Unit Profile.
effects: When Transmutation occurs, the first Unit Profile and its Model or representation are replaced by the second Unit Profile and corresponding Model or Token.
VITA or STR points and Wounds are shared across the user's Unit Profiles.
Applicable States are shared across the user's Unit Profiles.
Transmutation (X) changes to the second Unit Profile after the listed Wound threshold is reached.

Transmutation (Escape System-X) follows the threshold transition and also places an Eclipse Special Ammo Circular Template; if the Trooper is [[state:possessed|Possessed]] when it changes profile, [[state:possessed]] is canceled.
Transmutation (Hatching) begins with a Seed-Embryo representation and changes to the Developed Form when its documented Movement or successful [[skill:dodge]] ARO trigger occurs.
Transmutation (Auto) allows deployment in either Unit Profile and profile switching at the start of Movement generated by a Skill with the Movement Label.
Transmutation (WIP) allows a WIP Roll before an Order or ARO to use the second Unit Profile for the rest of the Player Turn, returning to the first profile in the States Phase.

records.name: Hacker
records.summary: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that identifies a Trooper as a Hacker, allowing [[equipment:hacking-device:plural]] and assigned Hacking Programs or Upgrades to provide their documented quantronic capabilities.

effects: A Hacker may use a [[equipment:hacking-device]] they are equipped with; the Device determines which Hacking Programs it grants.
A Hacker may instead have Hacking Programs assigned directly without requiring a [[equipment:hacking-device]].
Upgrade Programs may be assigned to the Hacker independently of the baseline Programs granted by a [[equipment:hacking-device]].
The Hacker Special Skill remains active while its owner is in a Null State.

records.name: Fireteams: General Rules
records.summary: The shared N5 rules for creating and operating Fireteams; Army-specific Fireteams Charts determine permitted teams and can override these defaults.

rules: The Army's Fireteams Chart determines how many Fireteams of each Type may exist and which Troopers or options may form them.
Members must observe Coherency with the Fireteam Leader, belong to the same Combat Group, and a Trooper cannot simultaneously belong to more than one Fireteam.
Spending a Regular Order on a Fireteam member makes that Trooper the Fireteam Leader and activates the other members of the Fireteam.
Army-chart conditions and notes can modify or override the general Fireteam rules.

terminology.meaning: Historical official shorthand for Fireteam participation. Current N5 eligibility is contextual to the Army Fireteams Chart rather than a universal Unit property.
Community shorthand rooted in earlier Fireteam Composition Bonuses. Current N5 instead uses Fireteam Level from same-Unit or chart-equivalent membership.

records.name: Fireteam Level and Bonuses
records.summary: Fireteam Level is calculated from same-Unit or chart-equivalent members and grants cumulative bonuses from Level 1 through Level 5.

facts.basis: Fireteam Level is based on how many members belong to the same Unit; matching bracketed or noted Fireteams Chart terms count as the same Unit for this calculation.

levels.requirement: The Troopers may all belong to different Units.
bonuses: Fireteam members activate with a single Regular Order.

levels.requirement: At least 2 Troopers belong to the same Unit.
At least 3 Troopers belong to the same Unit.
At least 4 Troopers belong to the same Unit.
All 5 Troopers belong to the same Unit.

records.name: Unit and Unit Profile
records.summary: A Unit groups Troopers belonging to an Army. A Unit Profile provides the data used for those Troopers and can contain multiple selectable options with different Skills, Equipment, Weapons, and Cost.

records.name: Attributes
records.summary: Attributes are the values in the profile statline. A dash means the game element does not have that Attribute; VITA and STR are alternative durability Attributes, and a dash for MOV means the Trooper is stationary.

records.name: Training and Orders
records.summary: Regular and Irregular are Training characteristics that determine the ordinary Order a Trooper contributes. Special Lieutenant Orders and Tactical Orders are separate generated Order types rather than additional Training values.

records.name: Troop Type
records.summary: Troop Type is a rules category such as LI, MI, HI, REM, TAG, WB, SK, VH, or Peripheral. It is a separate axis from Trooper Classification and can be referenced by rules restrictions.

records.name: Trooper Classification
records.summary: Trooper Classification describes a Unit’s function and operational role. It is distinct from Troop Type and can matter to Army composition in missions or scenarios.

records.name: ISC
records.summary: ISC is the International Standard Code, a language-independent name used for O-12 intelligence reporting.

records.name: Hackable
records.summary: Hackable is a Trooper Characteristic shown in the Unit Profile. Rules that affect Hackable targets use this characteristic to determine whether the target is eligible.

records.name: Peripheral
records.summary: A Peripheral is a special category of Trooper associated with a Controller. Unit Profile notation keeps Peripherals distinct from ordinary Weapons and Equipment instead of treating them as carried gear.

records.name: Skills
records.summary: Skills are rules listed on a Unit Profile that describe actions, capabilities, or effects available to a Trooper. A Skill can apply across a profile or only to a specific option.

records.name: Equipment
records.summary: Equipment is gear listed on a Unit Profile that provides rules or capabilities to a Trooper. Equipment can apply across a profile or only to a specific option.

records.name: Weapons
records.summary: Weapons are the attack options listed on a Unit Profile, including BS Weapons and close-combat weapons. A Weapon can apply across a profile or only to a specific option.

records.name: Profiles and Loadouts
records.summary: A Unit Profile shows shared abilities and gear. Individual loadouts show the selectable options, including any differences in Skills, Equipment, Weapons, [[skill:peripheral:plural]], [[attribute:swc|SWC]], and [[attribute:c|Cost]].

records.name: Normal (N) Ammunition
records.summary: Conventional Ammunition that uses the weapon’s listed Saving Roll Attribute and has no additional special effect.

records.name: Armor Piercing (AP) Ammunition
records.summary: Armor-piercing Ammunition that reduces the target’s applicable ARM or BTS value by half for its Saving Roll.

records.name: Double Action (DA) Ammunition
records.summary: High-impact Ammunition that requires two Saving Rolls for each successful hit.

records.name: Eclipse Ammunition
records.summary: A Smoke variant that creates a visibility-blocking zone which also affects [[equipment:multispectral-visor:plural]].

records.name: Electromagnetic (E/M) Ammunition
records.summary: Electromagnetic Ammunition that forces multiple reduced-BTS Saving Rolls and can disable affected targets.

records.name: Explosive (EXP) Ammunition
records.summary: Explosive Ammunition that requires three Saving Rolls for each successful hit.

records.name: Paralysis (PARA) Ammunition
records.summary: Non-lethal Ammunition that uses a modified PH Saving Roll and can immobilize affected targets.

records.name: Shock Ammunition
records.summary: Lethal Ammunition that can bypass incapacitation for vulnerable one-Vitality targets.

records.name: Smoke Ammunition
records.summary: Non-lethal Ammunition that creates a Zero Visibility Zone and can oppose attacks whose Line of Fire crosses it.

records.name: Stun Ammunition
records.summary: Non-lethal Ammunition that can impose a disabling effect and force the target to fail its subsequent Guts Roll.

records.name: T2 Ammunition
records.summary: High-damage Ammunition whose failed Saving Rolls normally inflict two Wounds.

records.name: Domination
records.summary: Core scenario using four scoring Quadrants and four Consoles.

sourceIssues.description: The Domination Forces and Deployment chart on N5.3 printed page 151 assigns 6 SWC to a 350-point game, while Annihilation assigns 7 SWC at the same Army Points. InfinityDB retains the scenario-specific printed value of 6 SWC. The difference may be intentional, but is noteworthy because the surrounding standard game-size progression would otherwise suggest 7.

records.name: Supplies
records.summary: Core scenario using three carryable Supply Boxes on the center line.

records.name: Annihilation
records.summary: Core scenario scored by enemy forces eliminated, surviving forces, and killing the enemy [[skill:lieutenant]].

sourceIssues.description: The 350-point surviving-Victory-Points column on printed page 149 appears to contain two typographical boundary errors: it prints 85–150 for 1 Objective Point and more than 250 for 4, while the surrounding progression and the corresponding enemy-kills column use contiguous bands. InfinityDB therefore uses the reviewed intended ranges 85–175, 176–270, and more than 270 for 1, 3, and 4 Objective Points respectively.

records.name: Firefight
records.summary: Core scenario using the standard opposing Deployment Zone map with scenario-specific combat objectives.

records.name: Dominate Quadrants
records.summary: Rules for Dominate Quadrants.

effects: Count dominated Quadrants at the end of each Game Round, never earlier. Their boundaries are shown in the selected map.
A player dominates a Quadrant by having more Victory Points inside it than the opponent. Count only Troopers represented by Models or Markers; Troopers classified as Null do not count.
Tokens and Markers for weapons, Equipment, or anything other than a Trooper do not contribute Victory Points.
A Trooper is inside a Quadrant only when more than half of its base lies within that Quadrant.
A Trooper with [[skill:shasvastii]] inside a Quadrant contributes its Points while [[state:normal|Normal]] or in its Shasvastii-Embryo form.

records.name: Consoles
records.summary: Rules for Consoles.

effects: Place one Console at the center of each of the four scoring Quadrants, using the maintained marker positions in the selected map.
Represent each Console with a Console A Marker or scenery of the same diameter.

records.name: Specialist Troops
records.summary: Skills that qualify a Trooper as a Specialist for the applicable scenario.

restrictions: [[skill:doctor:plural]] and [[skill:engineer:plural]] cannot use [[skill:peripheral:plural]] for tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.
The Non Specialist variant of [[skill:chain-of-command]] does not grant Specialist status through that Skill. Other qualifying Skills still apply.

records.name: Supply Boxes
records.summary: Rules for Supply Boxes.

effects: Place three Supply Boxes: one at the center of the table and two on its center line, at the positions shown in the selected map.
Represent each Supply Box with a Supply Box Marker or a similar scenery item.
Deployment in Silhouette contact with a Supply Box is not permitted.

records.name: Carrying Supply Boxes
records.summary: Rules for Carrying Supply Boxes.

effects: Each Specialist Troop may carry at most one Supply Box.
Only Models can carry Supply Boxes; Markers cannot carry them.
Keep the Supply Box Token on the table even if its carrier becomes classified as Null.

records.name: Controlling Supply Boxes
records.summary: Rules for Controlling Supply Boxes.

effects: At game end, a player controls a Supply Box only if one of their Models is carrying it. A Marker cannot control a Supply Box.
The carrier must not be classified as Null and must not be in Silhouette contact with any enemy Model.

records.name: Killing
records.summary: Rules for Killing.

effects: An enemy Trooper counts as killed after entering [[state:dead]] or if it is classified as Null when the game ends.
A Trooper that has never deployed on the table as a Model or Marker counts as killed when the game ends.

records.name: Reinforced Tactical Link
records.summary: Rules for Reinforced Tactical Link.

effects: For this mission, the identity of the [[skill:lieutenant]] is always Open Information. If represented by a Marker, identify which Marker is the [[skill:lieutenant]].
The [[skill:lieutenant]] must be on the game table at the beginning of the first Game Round, as a Model or Marker.

At the start of the Tactical Phase of your Active Turn, if you lack a [[skill:lieutenant]] because that Trooper was not deployed or is classified as Null, appoint a new [[skill:lieutenant]] without spending an Order.
The replacement [[skill:lieutenant]] must be a Model or Marker on the table, and its identity is also Open Information.

records.name: Designated Landing Area
records.summary: Rules for Designated Landing Area.

effects: The whole game table is a Designated Landing Area. A Trooper with [[skill:combat-jump]] may apply a +3 MOD to its deployment [[attribute:ph]] Roll.
This +3 MOD is cumulative with MODs provided by other rules.
A Trooper with a Special Skill carrying the Airborne Deployment (AD) Label ignores the prohibition against deploying inside the enemy Deployment Zone.

records.name: Hack Consoles
records.summary: A Short Skill used by Specialist Troops to Hack a Console.

requirements: Only Specialist Troops may declare this Skill.
The Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with a Console.
effects: A successful unopposed [[attribute:wip]] Roll Hacks the Console. A failed attempt may be repeated by spending another Short Skill and making another Roll.
A Console can be Hacked again after the opponent has Hacked it. Only the most recent player to Hack it counts the Console as Hacked.
A [[skill:hacker]] receives a +3 MOD to the unopposed [[attribute:wip]] Roll to Hack a Console.

records.name: Pick Up Supply Boxes
records.summary: A Short Skill used by Specialist Troops to collect a Supply Box.

requirements: Only Specialist Troops may declare this Skill.

The Specialist must be in Silhouette contact with a Supply Box Token not being carried by a Model, with any Model classified as Null carrying a Supply Box Token, or with an allied Model in [[state:normal|Normal]] carrying a Supply Box Token.
effects: Spend one Short Skill to pick up the Supply Box without making a Roll, following the common Supply Box rules.
restrictions: Follow the common Supply Box carrying and control rules for this scenario.

condition.text: If the active player finds that all Troopers in their Army List are classified as Null during their Tactical Phase, finish the mission at the end of that Player Turn.

During the active player’s Tactical Phase, total the Victory Points of Troopers in their Army List that are not classified as Null. If the total is below the minimum Victory Points in the selected game-size row, finish the mission at the end of that Player Turn.
